newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Gulf council chief hopes Bahrain attends meeting.
newsitem.headline: Gulf council chief hopes Bahrain attends meeting.

text.p: The Secretary-General of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) said on Sunday he was optimistic Bahrain would reconsider its decision to skip December's summit in Qatar, the official Kuwait News Agency reported.
"The GCC Secretary-General Jameel al-Hujailan said he was optimistic that the summit will be held with all members attending," said the agency in a dispatch from Riyadh.

Bahrain said on Wednesday it would not attend the summit in Qatar, which has taken a territorial dispute with the island state to the International Court of Justice. Bahrain wants an Arab Gulf solution to the dispute with Qatar.
However, Bahrain's Cabinet Affairs and Information Minister Mohammad Ibrahim al-Mutawae said on Thursday Manama might attend the summit if the problems prompting its boycott were removed.
A headline ran by Kuwait's al-Qabas newspaper on Sunday from an interview with Qatar's Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani, which will be published on Monday, read:
"(I am) ready to visit Bahrain in person and present an invitation to (Bahrain's) Sheikh Isa (bin Sulman al-Khalifa) to attend the Gulf summit."
In a report based on remarks by Hujailan, the agency said: "His (Hujailan) optimism...stems a felt keen interest of Council states' leaders on (safeguarding) the coherence of the council."
The GCC, which also groups Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar, Oman and the United Arab Emirates, is to hold its annual summit in the Qatari capital Doha on December 7.
